confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'That should have fixed the original problem... it is reasonable to use it again normally.' The drive belt was never inspected, and the brushbar stopped dead, which points to a snapped belt.

rationale: The first reply over-escalated with an engineer-only stop-use warning for what is a belt and jam problem, then the final reply reversed that and said the vacuum could be used again. It never asked the customer to remove the sole plate and check the belt, even though the brushbar had stopped dead and the belt was the obvious suspect. The customer was left without the real fix (a new drive belt for the U85-AS-Be, with the model number needed to choose it), and was only told to come back if it still failed. The advice also contradicts itself, since it first said not to use the vacuum even after clearing the roller and later said it was fine to use.</br>
